C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: moduleTopology
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The module topology, for a module `A` over a topological ring `R`. It's the finest topology
making addition and the `R`-action continuous, or equivalently the finest topology making `A`
into a topological `R`-module. More precisely it's the Inf of the set of
topologies with these properties; theorems `continuousSMul` and `continuousAdd` show
that the module topology also has these properties. -/
abbrev moduleTopology : TopologicalSpace A :=
  sInf {t | @ContinuousSMul R A _ _ t ∧ @ContinuousAdd A t _}
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/-- The module topology, for a module `A` over a topological ring `R`. It's the finest topology

into a topological `R`-module. More precisely it's the Inf of the set of
topologies with these properties; theorems `continuousSMul` and `continuousAdd` show
that the module topology also has these properties. -/
abbrev moduleTopology : TopologicalSpace A :=
  sInf {t | @ContinuousSMul R A _ _ t ∧ @ContinuousAdd A t _}

rag.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.mul_assoc
rag.content:
protected theorem mul_assoc (x y z : A ⊗[R] B) : mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z) := by
  -- restate as an equality of morphisms so that we can use `ext`
  suffices LinearMap.llcomp R _ _ _ mul ∘ₗ mul =
      (LinearMap.llcomp R _ _ _ LinearMap.lflip <| LinearMap.llcomp R _ _ _ mul.flip ∘ₗ mul).flip by
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun (DFunLike.congr_fun (DFunLike.congr_fun this x) y) z
  ext xa xb ya yb za zb
  exact congr_arg₂ (· ⊗ₜ ·) (mul_assoc xa ya za) (mul_assoc xb yb zb)

The abbreviation Dfx represents the group of units of the tensor product between D and the ring of finite adeles over the ring of integers of a field K, with respect to K.

/-

# Fujisaki's lemma

We prove a lemma which Voight (in his quaternion algebra book) attributes to Fujisaki:
if `D` is a finite-dimensional division algebra over a number field `K`
and if `U ⊆ (D ⊗[K] 𝔸_K^infty)ˣ` is a compact open subgroup then the double coset
space `Dˣ \ (D ⊗[K] 𝔸_K^infty)ˣ / U` is finite.

-/

C1_dependencies.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- `S ⊗[R] T` has a `T`-algebra structure. This is not a global instance or else the action of
`S` on `S ⊗[R] S` would be ambiguous. -/
abbrev rightAlgebra : Algebra B (A ⊗[R] B) :=
  includeRight.toRingHom.toAlgebra' fun b x => by
    suffices LinearMap.mulLeft R (includeRight b) = LinearMap.mulRight R (includeRight b) from
      congr($this x)
    ext xa xb
    simp [mul_comm]
